decisions.reason: Although it fit the consumer-health portfolio and could be tolerated for a time because the firm has slack, its visibility appears limited to the first two years after launch, suggesting results stayed below aspiration and resources are better redeployed.

The product received launch support but shows no sign of sustained prominence beyond the early period, so under a boundedly rational portfolio review it likely underperformed aspiration and should be discontinued.

Its move from a mention to its own page indicates an initial trial, but the lack of continued evidence by 2022 implies the experiment did not meet aspiration levels strongly enough to justify keeping it.

Despite being presented as innovative and temporarily benefiting from the firm's willingness to broaden its supplement line, the weak longer-run signal points to insufficient performance relative to aspiration.

A generic product already marked by a public valsartan-related problem threatens quality reputation and, without stronger signs of continued support, falls below aspiration enough to trigger reallocation of resources.
As a more distant launch with only initial website support and no clear evidence of sustained traction, it likely remained too uncertain relative to aspiration to keep in the portfolio by 2022.
